extracted.intended_audience: investigators preparing NIH R01 (PA-20-185) biomedical research grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: A complete sample NIH Research Project Grant (Parent R01, Clinical Trial Not Allowed) application showing required forms, plans, institutional resources, and compliance statements that applicants must provide when applying for NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIAID posts new samples periodically (link provided). Samples demonstrate good grantsmanship but may not reflect latest format or rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF424 / Certifications and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I also provide the required assurances and agree to comply with any resulting terms if I accept an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing party is aware that false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements or claims may subject them to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to character/length restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not exceed character length restrictions indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form instructions and section-specific length limits must be followed (e.g., title length limit noted: 'Do not exceed 81 characters').

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether human subjects are involved; if yes, indicate whether the project is Exempt (and exemption number) or whether IRB review is pending/approved and provide IRB approval date and Human Subject Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also specify clinical trial status (NIH-defined Phase III) where applicable. Provide Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used; if yes, indicate whether IACUC review is pending/approved and provide IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe animal facility accreditation (e.g., AAALAC) and IACUC protocol identifiers where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of proprietary/privileged information and environmental/historic impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether proprietary/privileged information is included, whether the project has an actual or potential environmental impact, and whether the performance site is designated or eligible as a historic place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes to environmental impact, provide explanation and note if an environmental assessment (EA) or EIS has been performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project period and funding request fields (SF424 specifics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proposed project start/end dates and estimated project funding (federal and non-federal) for each budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all SF424 fields including applicant organization identification, authorized representative signature, and contact information for PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe laboratory, office, animal facility, computer resources, core facilities, and other institutional resources available to support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include square footage, bench/office allocations, shared resources, access to core instrumentation (sequencing, microscopy, proteomics), seminar/training environment, and administrative support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biosafety level statement
rubrics_metrics.description: State the biosafety level of the laboratory (e.g., BSL-2) and describe biosafety practices and personnel training; indicate that no select agents will be employed if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm compliance with Institutional Biosafety Officers and relevant biosafety protocols for handling biohazardous agents described in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment availability and listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List all major equipment available to conduct the proposed work (freezers, incubators, centrifuges, qPCR systems, plate readers, flow cytometers, robotic platforms, microscopes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide equipment details by laboratory/room and indicate access to institutional/shared equipment and cores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe institutional scientific environment and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the scientific environment, collaborative opportunities, biostatistics support, translational research infrastructure (CTSA/VICTR), and institutional track record that will contribute to project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention availability of data capture systems (e.g., REDCap), web portals for research administration (e.g., StarBRITE), and access to genomics/biostatistics cores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for Intellectual Property and Sharing of Research Resources: intellectual property and data generated under this project will be administered in accordance with both University and NIH policies, including the NIH Data Sharing Policy and Implementation Guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership of inventions will follow U.S. patent law (Title 35 USC); inventors and institutions must disclose inventions and manage them per NIH/university policies; materials may be transferred under MTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access, timing, and de-identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to databases and associated software tools generated under the project will be available for educational, research and non-profit purposes; research data which documents, supports and validates findings will be made available after the main findings from the final research data set have been accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide web-based access as appropriate and redact personal identifiers prior to data release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to NIH Grant Policy on Sharing of Unique Research Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to NIH Grant Policy on Sharing of Unique Research Resources and Principles and Guidelines for Recipients of NIH Grants and Contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make protocols and mutants generated available to other researchers upon request, and distribute materials per NIH guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing model organisms requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Model organisms generated by the project will be distributed widely or deposited into a repository/stock center making them available to the broader research community, either before or immediately after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If responsible for distribution, fill requests in a timely fashion; provide relevant protocols and published genetic and phenotypic data upon request; material transfers made with no more restrictive terms than the Simple Letter Agreement (SLA) or the Uniform Biological Materials Transfer Agreement (UBMTA) and without reach-through requirements; ensure technology remains widely available even if patenting occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Plans attachment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Other Plan(s) attachment included with the application is not evaluated during the peer review process but will be evaluated prior to a funding decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other Plans is maintained as a separate document in eRA Commons viewable by authorized users and is not part of the assembled application for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources (header requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources plan describing how key materials will be authenticated and quality-controlled during the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This header requires specific authentication steps for cultured cells, mice, DNA constructs, bacterial strains, and other critical reagents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate cultured cell lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain cultured cells (primary or cell lines) in culture with banks (e.g., frozen when first obtained) and routinely screen cell cultures for microbial contamination (yeast, gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria) using a contamination detection kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep cell banks in liquid nitrogen; document provenance and screening procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate mice and animal sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain mice (including humanized strains) from reputable vendors (e.g., Jackson Laboratory or CFAR animal core); if acquired from collaborators, confirm by SNP scanning services or track genotypes via standard mouse genotyping protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of vendor/source, genotyping, and animal care; reference approved IACUC protocol identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify DNA constructs by sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: All DNA constructs generated during the course of the project will be verified by sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep sequence verification records and ensure constructs match intended designs before use in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bacterial strain handling and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: S. aureus strains used for the study were or will be frozen at -80°C on first acquisition. For all experiments, streaks of the original frozen stocks will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track strain provenance, storage conditions, and usage to ensure reproducibility and avoid drift/contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material transfer and distribution terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials generated under the project may be transferred to others under the terms of a material transfer agreement; transfers should not be more restrictive than SLA or UBMTA and should avoid reach-through requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to use standard institutional MTAs and to deposit materials in repositories when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and confidentiality protections
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH responds to FOIA requests for grant applications and summary statements, the material will be subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions. NIH must protect all confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should recognize that some portions of applications may be redacted if released under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance / accessibility note
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications/samples may be reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology; contact provided for accessibility issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trouble accessing content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.
